text: This is Root Cause. A debugger for football.
Pick a match, like this four all thriller between West London Blues and Manchester Sky Blues. Eight goals. Four of them traced to the mistake behind them.
Take the twenty-eighth minute. A corner, a header, one all.
Root Cause reconstructs the move on a three D pitch, then walks back from the goal, second by second.
The yellow line is the defending back line. Watch who drops behind it.
At every touch, it asks one question. What let this happen?
Seven seconds before the goal, centre back Manuel Akendo is five point three metres behind his line.
A second defender, Diales, is out of position too. Two suspects. So which one cost the goal?
Root Cause runs the experiment. Fix one mistake, then replay the attack two hundred times.
As played, seventy one percent of replays end in a goal. With Akendo level, just seven percent. Fix Diales instead, fifty nine.
Verdict: Akendo carries eighty four percent of the blame. Measured, not guessed.
The same evidence, told your way. Simple for fans. Expert for analysts.
In English, Hindi and Spanish. And the Tactics Lab opens up all ninety minutes: space, passing options, pressure and runs.
Root Cause. Every goal has a bug.
